brief: A dovish trifecta this week, soft jobs, tame PCE and the G7 oil release, has shifted odds toward a Fed pause and eventual easing, easing diesel and inflation pressure and supporting duration, real assets and hard money. Record index levels mask heavy internal dispersion: homebuilders down 15-20% in a month, semis-vs-software whipsaws, hard-to-manage shorts and crowding, while mega-cap concentration drives the tape (Nvidia near $6 trillion, Meta's rally, Microsoft up 50% from July lows). Because belief in AI and AI capex holds, equities are treated as largely detached from oil, rates, jobs and geopolitics; the three pillars now are yields, oil and the AI theme. US and UK 30-year yields sit near 6.25%, the highest since 2002 and 1998 respectively, and French OATs just had their worst quarter since the euro's creation, with the ECB's TPI backstop possibly excluded given 2027 elections. AI capex is likened to past bubbles (railways, utilities, Japan, dotcom, shale) where the trigger is always a central bank pivot; AI names are 42% of S&P cap versus 40-44% in prior manias, VC rounds reprice within weeks, and data-center build-out likely caps at 20-25 GW on delays. IPO issuance is pausing as liquidity discernment rises.
